newsitem.title: USA: Senate rejects last-minute school repair strategy.
newsitem.headline: Senate rejects last-minute school repair strategy.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Thursday rejected a proposal to include a $5 billion school infrastructure spending plan in the balanced budget agreement.
Senators voted 56-43 to table a motion by Sen. Carol Moseley-Braun, D-N.Y., to bring the issue up for a vote as the Senate takes final action on the landmark budget pact.

The school construction measure originally was included in President Clinton's fiscal 1998 proposed budget, but it was dropped three weeks ago during negotiations between the White House and Republican leaders on the budget deal.
"This is not the end of the game," a Moseley-Braun aide said after Thursday's vote. The senator is "exploring other options," including alternative financing mechanisms, the aide said.
"It probably wouldn't be direct payments" by the federal government, the aide said. "It may be some kind of loan assistance like we have for student or housing loans," the aide said.
The aide said Mosely-Braun has received "private assurances" from Clinton that he still favors enactment of school construction legislation.
In related action, Democratic leaders on Thursday demanded that the Republican Congress adopt a "pro-education agenda" that includes funding for construction and repair of school buildings.

The Democrats said in a press statement that the budget agreement already includes provisions for Pell Grants, Head Start, child literacy, bilingual and immigrant education, and educational technology.
They pledged to "work tirelessly throughout the rest of this Congress" to enact legislation that funds school infastructure improvements and other remaining issues, the statement said.
